subject: C15
required_fixes: R2 (remaining) — Validate the complete effective header set for registered-origin requests. crates/desktop-core/src/workbench/admission.rs:393 checks only plan.headers for Host/forwarding overrides, while execute.rs:383 later creates a header from Auth::ApiKey.name. Consequently [auth] kind="api-key", name="Host", secret="host-value" bypasses the new Host rejection at a registered Prisma destination. The non-managed branch at admission.rs:516 also accepts literal method-override headers and conflicting/duplicate Authorization sources; it does not apply the managed branch's ambiguity checks. For example, a catalogued GET with X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE is admitted as a read and forwarded unchanged. Actual service handling of override headers was not live-tested; admitting them already violates the conservative method/authority contract. Acceptance: before secret resolution or dispatch, reject Host/forwarding and method overrides supplied through either editor headers or generated auth headers, and reject conflicting/duplicate authentication at registered origins. Preserve one valid manual Authorization source and ordinary unregistered HTTP. Add literal production-interface fixtures for these paths, including generated Host and method-override headers.

R5 — Registered-origin mutation reviews are not bound to the authentication and cookie state actually sent. In crates/desktop-core/src/authority/workbench_domain/send.rs:455, the digest reduces Basic and Bearer auth to other.kind(); it omits Basic username and both kinds' secret references. Changing a literal Basic username or switching the direct Bearer secret reference therefore leaves the digest unchanged. Collection secrets are replaced under the same deterministic record ID (workbench_domain.rs:2316; workbench/profile.rs:51), with no credential revision bound to the review. Cookies are absent from the digest and loaded only at send.rs:1063; execute.rs:782 reads the current mutable jar. A secret replacement, cookie-clearing action or intervening Set-Cookie response can consequently change the credential/account used by an already approved mutation. This violates DESIGN.md's explicit auth, credential-revision and cookie-snapshot bindings. Acceptance: changing Basic username, Basic/Bearer secret reference, a referenced collection secret's revision, or effective cookies after review must require a fresh review and send nothing under the old approval, including changes while native confirmation is held. Bind and recheck these inputs without exposing secret values; transmit the same admitted cookie/auth snapshot rather than reading mutable values later.
optional_suggestions: Retarget the surviving 'tenant redirects are followed' mutation probe to an unregistered loopback destination. Its current same-origin target is independently blocked by the registered-origin redirect guard, so changing Managed => false to true survives the fixture suite. The retained results correctly show 39 of 40 probes killed; this probe does not isolate the managed redirect rule.

Findings are source-traced; their proposed negative fixtures have not been executed by this reviewer.
